name: char_retarget_map
description: How animation sources become clips on the shared skeleton. Every mapping here is between a source's bone naming and the names in char_skeleton_definition.json; nothing retargets bone-to-bone by position, because positional retargeting silently mangles proportions.

sources.status_note: VERIFIED against the pack. The first version of this map used Mixamo names (LeftUpLeg, Spine1, LeftArm) on the assumption that Quaternius followed that convention. It does not: the UAL rig uses Unreal-mannequin names. The retarget_bones probe measured joints_in_glb=65 against mapped_names=23 and matched exactly ONE of them (Head), which is the only name both conventions happen to share — so every other entry named a bone that does not exist and retargeting would have silently done nothing. This file is now written from the pack's measured joints and the probe reports matched=23 of 23, unmatched=[]. What is still NOT verified is retargeting itself: no clip has been retargeted onto the target skeleton yet. That is Phase 5.
sources.known_naming: Unreal-mannequin convention, confirmed by measurement: `pelvis`, `spine_01..03`, `neck_01`, `Head`, `clavicle_l`, `upperarm_l`, `lowerarm_l`, `hand_l`, `thigh_l`, `calf_l`, `foot_l`, `ball_l`, and the same with `_r`. Note `Head` is capitalised and the rest are not — that is the pack's naming, not a typo. The rig also carries `*_leaf` bones (ball_leaf, index_04_leaf, and so on), which are leaf/twist helpers and are dropped rather than mapped.
sources.rest_pose: T-pose, matching the target rest pose, so no rest-pose correction is needed.
sources.scale: Quaternius characters are authored around 1.8 m. Reject any clip whose root height differs by more than 5 % from the target skeleton before retargeting.

evidence.note: Every entry below is now confirmed against the pack's real skin joints. The first rewrite of this map was written partly from the standard Unreal chain because the probe truncated its joint sample to 25 names; the next run printed all 65 and the probe matched all 23 entries, so nothing here is inferred any more.

fingers.reason: The pack does carry finger chains — `thumb_01_l`, `index_01_l` through `index_04_leaf_l`, and the same for middle, ring and pinky — but finger animation is invisible at the distances this game shows characters, and mapping 40 extra joints onto a 56-bone target would blow the bone budget. Fingers are posed by a static grip clip per weapon type instead.
fingers.source_finger_names: thumb_01..03 plus thumb_04_leaf, index_01..03 plus index_04_leaf, and the same for middle, ring and pinky — each with _l and _r, 40 joints in total

sources.unmapped_source_bones: Any source bone not listed here is dropped, not guessed at. That is deliberate and it is a lot of bones: the 40 finger joints and every `*_leaf` helper. The retarget report lists what was dropped so a missing jaw or eye bone is visible rather than silent — and note the pack has NO jaw or eye bones, so facial animation cannot come from it at all.

sources.status_note: Not implemented and not tested. Every clip the packs cannot supply is to be authored with bpy against the target skeleton directly, so it needs no retarget map. This is a plan for Phase 5, not a working generator: the 27 animation families Quaternius does not cover depend on it (measured, not estimated — see the quaternius_coverage line in reports/tool_evaluation.md, which is the live figure and will move as the matcher changes).
sources.reason: Every clip the packs cannot supply is authored with bpy against the target skeleton directly, so it needs no retarget map at all. This is the fallback for the whole animation list if the release never appears.

rules: Retarget by bone name, never by position or hierarchy inference.
No scale keys survive retargeting: a clip with scale channels is rejected, per the brief.
Every clip is resampled to 30 fps on the way in, using glTF-Transform's resample, so a 60 fps source does not double the file size.

Locomotion clips record their root speed in metres per second in the clip's metadata, so gameplay can match animation speed to movement speed and foot-sliding is measurable rather than a matter of opinion.
A loop clip's first and last frame must agree within 1 degree of rotation and 1 cm of position. The validator measures this on the exported GLB, not on the source file.
Clips are stored one per GLB animation, named exactly as in the manifest's anims[] list, so a missing or renamed clip fails the validator instead of silently doing nothing at runtime.

root_speed_metadata.note: Measured from the root bone's horizontal displacement over the clip, divided by its duration. Written into the GLB's extras for the clip.
